correctness.rationale: The primary source proves that the half-edge lengths are \(\ell_k=\|Aq_k\|\) for an orthonormal frame. Writing \(B=A^2\), Hadamard gives \(\det B\le\prod q_k^{\mathsf T}Bq_k\), with equality exactly in an eigenbasis, while arithmetic-geometric mean and \(\operatorname{tr}B=1\) give the universal upper product \(n^{-n}\). An inductive Rayleigh-quotient argument proves that a constant-diagonal orthonormal basis always exists, so the upper endpoint is genuinely attained by a regular cube. Connectedness gives the full interval, and the polar determinant formula gives the reciprocal cross-polytope interval and constant volume product.

value.rationale: The source produces an \(O(n)\)-sized family of higher-dimensional Poncelet/Fuss parallelotopes but does not quantify how a basic geometric invariant varies across that family. The result determines the complete volume spectrum in every dimension, identifies both equality mechanisms, and yields the structural corollary that every admissible anisotropic inner ellipsoid admits a tight regular cube. The polar statement simultaneously gives the exact dual cross-polytope spectrum and a constant primal-dual volume product. This is a natural family-wide extremal theorem rather than a numerical computation for a fixed ellipsoid.
